k0_2_semantic_rows.coverage_rule: Every configuration, enum, operation, and callable-helper semantic ID appears exactly once in semantic_coverage; context-only classification does not discard its retry, timeout, cancellation, shutdown, or resource-bound authority.

k1_2_negotiation_transitions.evidence_rule: Protocol negotiation, correlation, disconnect, reconnect, and drift cells remain blocking target-policy context, not current lifecycle proof.

k1_2_protocol_binding_groups.coverage_limitation: K1.2 binding groups are cross-slice context only and are not exhaustive lifecycle coverage; K1.4 resolves direct K0.2 semantic IDs independently.

classifications.reason: All 43 configuration rows carry resource-bound authority; timer and retry settings remain configuration facts rather than runtime guarantees.
These 26 operation rows carry direct resource or lifecycle ownership authority and are joined by source_authority_ids to at least one declared resource or lifecycle row.

These 28 enum, helper, validation, value-construction, diagnostic, and accessor rows remain exact semantic authority but do not independently acquire a long-lived resource or operation owner. Their fields are not promoted to runtime evidence.

resource_limit_dimensions.unit: records admitted to the dependency delivery queue
payload topic key header framing and queue bytes retained for admitted records
key topic and header bytes per returned record
offset entries per admitted commit call
aggregate nonempty topic bytes per admitted commit call
topic bytes retained by offset and position maps
topic bytes retained by the diagnostic consumer
closures holding one consumer broker_ops mutex

policy.numeric_rule: Every resource row names a unit and current plus required default, minimum, and maximum-or-hard-cap fields. A null numeric value is admissible only with an explicit blocking state; it is never interpreted as zero, unlimited, supported, or dependency parity.
policy.resource_semantic_binding_rule: Every RESOURCE-classified K0.2 semantic row maps to at least one declared resource row; timer configuration maps to its standalone timer budget rather than blanket prose.
policy.composite_dimension_rule: A resource class spanning incompatible units has explicit per-unit resource_limit_dimensions; its aggregate scalar row cannot substitute for those dimensions.
policy.incumbent_rule: Unbounded, inert, platform-width, dependency-owned, or source-ambiguous incumbent behavior remains a blocking gap and is not normalized into a native guarantee.
policy.admission_rule: Admission, backpressure, overflow, release, owner scope, and accounting invariants are distinct required fields; one cannot stand in for another.
policy.backpressure_field_rule: Each resource row's overflow_behavior field records the incumbent wait, reject, shed, overwrite, allocate, inline-execute, or dependency-unknown backpressure and overflow behavior; absence of a typed bounded outcome remains blocking.
policy.transition_rule: Every lifecycle operation carries timeout, cancellation, shutdown, panic, retry, restart, and ambiguous-outcome transitions over an explicit state set.
policy.cx_rule: A Cx entry checkpoint is not cancellation completion. Blocking calls, dependency callbacks, queued work, and post-effect continuations require independent certainty and release evidence.
policy.quiescence_rule: A closed flag, dropped handle, empty local map, or dependency callback is not quiescence evidence without owner-complete accounting and terminal lifecycle receipts.

resource_classes.unit: live broker connections
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Construction delegates connection creation and pooling to the native dependency without repository-visible admission accounting.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Future per-Cx client and broker-endpoint pool; incumbent dependency process state is not region-owned.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Unknown dependency behavior; no local typed saturation outcome.
resource_classes.release_point: Dependency object drop only; no checked drain or connection-close receipt.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Every admitted connection must have one owner and one terminal release receipt before Cx quiescence can be claimed.

resource_classes.unit: admitted requests awaiting terminal correlation
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Native request admission is dependency-owned; wrapper calls expose no common bounded request permit.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Future connection-scoped correlation table plus operation-scoped receipt owner.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Unknown; no typed full, wait, shed, or deadline outcome is frozen.
resource_classes.release_point: Matched response, definitive rejection, disconnect invalidation, or explicit ambiguous receipt transfer.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: admitted = terminal_definitive + terminal_ambiguous + currently_owned; correlation identities are unique per live connection.

resource_classes.unit: cached broker, leader, controller, and coordinator entries
resource_classes.admission_outcome: No first-party metadata cache exists; dependency policy is not statically surfaced.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Future Cx-owned client with connection-epoch-scoped routing entries.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Unknown; stale eviction and refresh pressure are dependency-owned.
resource_classes.release_point: Connection epoch invalidation, bounded eviction, client close, or region teardown.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: No routing entry outlives its connection epoch or remains ownerless after invalidation.

resource_classes.unit: payload bytes per submitted record
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Payloads above max_message_size return MessageTooLarge before enqueue; zero configured cap is rejected by validation.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Producer instance configuration and each submitted record.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Only payload bytes are rejected; encoded overhead is not included.
resource_classes.release_point: Immediate rejection or terminal delivery callback/local-model publication completion.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Owned payload bytes must be charged exactly once until terminal delivery certainty is transferred or resolved.

resource_classes.unit: aggregate encoded bytes and header entries per record
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Topic trim emptiness is checked, but topic bytes, key bytes, header count, header bytes, and framing overhead have no aggregate local admission cap.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Producer or transaction record until definitive or ambiguous delivery ownership transfer.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Allocation or dependency rejection; no local typed capacity outcome.
resource_classes.release_point: Immediate rejection, terminal callback, deterministic publication, or explicit ambiguous receipt owner.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: All encoded components must contribute to one charged record budget without double release.

resource_classes.unit: configured target bytes per batch
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Validation rejects zero, but repository code does not own or meter the native batch accumulator.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Future per-partition accumulator within one producer Cx scope.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Dependency-owned; no local wait, split, flush, or reject outcome.
resource_classes.release_point: Batch send completion, split/rejection, partition drain, or producer shutdown.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Sum of queued record charges equals accumulator charge plus records in terminal handoff.

resource_classes.unit: records and aggregate bytes admitted but not terminally accounted
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Immediate dependency queue rejection may retry and eventually returns QueueFull or a coarse error; no Cx-owned permit controls admission.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Producer instance, partition queue, and per-call delivery receipt.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Dependency error after possible wrapper retry; waiting versus rejection is not a stable public contract.
resource_classes.release_point: Definitive callback, immediate terminal rejection, or explicit ambiguous delivery receipt transfer.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Every successful enqueue contributes one live receipt until exactly one definitive or ambiguous terminal state.

resource_classes.unit: configured retries after the initial submission attempt
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Retryable immediate enqueue failures consume the local count; dependency retries can also occur independently.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One producer submission plus dependency request state.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Very large configured counts are accepted; total time and dependency retry composition are not bounded locally.
resource_classes.release_point: Successful enqueue handoff, nonretryable failure, count exhaustion, cancellation, or shutdown.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Each attempt consumes exactly one attempt token and cannot outlive the owning operation receipt.

resource_classes.unit: milliseconds of configured request timeout
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Every Rust Duration is accepted; the value is passed to native request.timeout.ms but does not directly bound the wrapper send await or compose one end-to-end deadline.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One operation deadline shared across admission, queue wait, broker work, retry, and terminal receipt.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Extreme durations are accepted and no uniform saturation rule is frozen.
resource_classes.release_point: Definitive completion, typed timeout with certainty, cancellation handoff, or shutdown handoff.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Retry and queue time consume the same monotonic operation deadline; no phase resets the budget silently.

resource_classes.unit: admitted producer operations
resource_classes.admission_outcome: A double-checked atomic counter rejects a close race, but it does not impose a concurrency cap.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Producer object; not a Cx region ledger.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: No explicit saturation or overflow outcome is frozen.
resource_classes.release_point: Operation guard drop after wrapper completion, caller future cancellation or drop, unwind after admission, or rejected close race; dependency-visible delivery can remain live after the wrapper guard releases.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: active equals admitted guards not yet dropped; close drain must observe zero without admitting new guards.

resource_classes.unit: retained records and aggregate retained bytes
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Accepted deterministic records append to process-global per-topic vectors without count or byte admission.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Process-global deterministic test model, not a production Cx scope.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Allocation growth or panic; no typed capacity result.
resource_classes.release_point: Test-only reset or process teardown; publication does not release storage.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: All retained records and bytes are attributable to an explicit test-model owner and reset boundary.

resource_classes.unit: live transaction handles per transactional producer
resource_classes.admission_outcome: State checks intend one Active handle, but begin and recovery are not single-flight and can admit duplicate work or handles.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Transactional producer Cx scope with exactly one handle owner or recovery owner.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Current races can duplicate handles or strand Active; no typed capacity outcome.
resource_classes.release_point: Definitive commit, definitive abort, or transfer to a single recovery obligation.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: idle + live_handle + finalizing_owner + recovery_owner = exactly one phase owner.

resource_classes.unit: staged records and aggregate staged bytes per transaction
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Payload-only checks apply, but record count and aggregate encoded bytes are uncapped.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One transaction handle and its producer partitions.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Allocation or dependency failure; no typed transaction-capacity outcome.
resource_classes.release_point: Commit, abort, failed-begin cleanup, or recovery ownership transfer.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Every staged record is charged to exactly one live transaction until one terminal disposition.

resource_classes.unit: coordinator, enrolled partition, and enrolled offset entries
resource_classes.admission_outcome: The wrapper exposes no first-party coordinator or enrollment ledger and cannot meter dependency-owned state.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Transaction epoch scoped to one transactional producer identity.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Unknown dependency behavior; no local typed capacity outcome.
resource_classes.release_point: Definitive end-transaction outcome, fencing, abort recovery, or producer shutdown residue receipt.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: No enrolled partition or offset survives its owning transaction epoch without an explicit recovery obligation.

resource_classes.unit: retained subscription topic strings and bytes
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Subscribe validates nonempty unique names but not topic count or aggregate bytes.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Consumer group member and subscription epoch.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Allocation or dependency failure; no local typed capacity outcome.
resource_classes.release_point: Successful replacement, successful close cleanup, or explicit failed-close residue owner.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Every retained topic belongs to exactly one current subscription epoch or one residue receipt.

resource_classes.unit: assigned or revoked topic-partition entries plus one generation scalar
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Assignment input validates uniqueness and nonnegative fields but not partition count or topic bytes.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Consumer member epoch and rebalance generation.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Collections allocate without a local cap; generation saturates at u64::MAX without a typed terminal state.
resource_classes.release_point: Revocation drain, replacement assignment, close cleanup, or explicit residue owner.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: A partition has at most one live local owner per generation; revoked work reaches a terminal state before reassignment.

resource_classes.unit: completed poll outcomes retained between blocking slice and caller
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Every poll shares one slot; concurrent completed slices can overwrite an unconsumed outcome.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Current implementation is consumer-global; target must bind each outcome to one poll receipt and assignment epoch.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Silent replacement can remove a record or error from application observation.
resource_classes.release_point: Consumption by the matching poll, explicit stale-epoch rejection, cancellation transfer, or close residue accounting.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Every produced poll outcome is consumed or explicitly discarded exactly once; overwrite is forbidden.

resource_classes.unit: copied record, key, payload, topic, and header bytes
resource_classes.admission_outcome: fetch_max_bytes defaults to 52428800 and max_poll_records to 500, but neither is a proven local copy or returned-batch cap; max_poll_records is inert.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Poll receipt, partition queue, and caller-owned returned record.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Allocation growth or dependency failure; no local typed capacity outcome.
resource_classes.release_point: Caller record drop, stale-epoch rejection, bounded queue drain, or shutdown residue accounting.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Fetched bytes transfer from connection budget to exactly one queue or caller owner and release once.

resource_classes.unit: offset entries and aggregate topic bytes per commit call
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Empty, duplicate, invalid, unassigned, or regressing batches reject; count and aggregate bytes are uncapped and cloned per retry.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One commit operation, group generation, and assignment epoch.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Allocation growth or broker failure; no local typed capacity outcome.
resource_classes.release_point: Definitive commit, typed ambiguous receipt transfer, terminal rejection, cancellation, or shutdown handoff.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Every admitted offset entry has one operation owner and cannot commit under a stale assignment epoch.

resource_classes.unit: topic-partition offset or position entries plus topic bytes
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Entries arise from poll, seek, or commit continuations; old topics can remain until successful close.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Consumer assignment epoch and explicit offset-policy owner.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Allocation growth; no eviction or typed capacity outcome.
resource_classes.release_point: Revocation-safe eviction, subscription replacement, successful close, or explicit residue owner.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: No map entry survives revocation or epoch replacement without a named recovery purpose.

resource_classes.unit: configured retries after the initial commit attempt
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Only commit_offsets uses this retry field; each retry reclones the unbounded caller batch.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One commit operation and assignment epoch.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Very large counts are accepted; total work, batch bytes, and elapsed time are not capped together.
resource_classes.release_point: Definitive completion, nonretryable failure, exhaustion, cancellation, or shutdown.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Each attempt consumes one token under one total deadline and revalidates ownership before effects.

resource_classes.unit: accepted blocking tasks awaiting or occupying workers
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Configured pool worker concurrency is finite, but accepted pending work enters an uncapped SegQueue and can remain retained after worker-spawn failure.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Cx blocking pool and the originating Kafka operation receipt.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: No pending-queue backpressure; shutdown rejection becomes a bridge panic in current callers.
resource_classes.release_point: Queued cancellation skip, completed closure/result handoff, explicit rejection, panic accounting, or pool shutdown drain.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: accepted = pending + running + terminal; every task retains its originating operation owner until terminal handoff.

resource_classes.unit: successfully spawned fallback blocking threads
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Slots below 256 can spawn an OS thread; saturation makes callers wait, and OS spawn failure runs the blocking closure inline on the async worker.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Process-global fallback counter rather than the originating Cx region.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Wait rather than reject at cap; inline execution on spawn failure changes the execution owner.
resource_classes.release_point: Thread closure completion and counter decrement; caller cancellation does not stop an already-started closure.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Global running count never exceeds 256 and every decrement corresponds to one prior successful increment; this alone is not Cx quiescence.

resource_classes.unit: callers waiting for a fallback thread slot
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Every excess caller waits by yielding; there is no bounded waiter permit or typed saturation result.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Process-global fallback bridge, not the originating operation Cx.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Unbounded waiter growth and scheduler work rather than rejection.
resource_classes.release_point: Slot acquisition, caller future drop, or runtime teardown; no explicit waiter ledger exists.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Every waiter is owned, cancellable by its operation Cx, and removed exactly once before quiescence.

resource_classes.unit: retained configuration scalars, strings, bytes, labels, and diagnostic records
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Configuration scalars and strings are retained without one aggregate budget; dependency error strings can be arbitrarily long, and diagnostics have no common byte, count, cardinality, or retention budget.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Operation receipt, client diagnostics owner, and bounded observability sink.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Allocation growth, unbounded cardinality, or sink-defined behavior; no typed local result.
resource_classes.release_point: Receipt consumption, bounded eviction, client close, or explicit retained-residue handoff.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Every retained diagnostic has a byte/cardinality charge, expiry, privacy class, and exactly one owner.

resource_classes.unit: dependency-owned threads, callbacks, queues, and retained client tasks
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Construction delegates background resource admission to the native dependency without Cx region accounting.
resource_classes.owner_scope: Incumbent native client lifetime; target must attach all background work to a client Cx scope.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Unknown dependency behavior; no local typed saturation outcome.
resource_classes.release_point: Dependency drop is the only observed boundary and is not a terminal drain receipt.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: No callback, queue entry, thread, timer, or client task remains after the owning Cx reaches quiescence.

resource_classes.unit: milliseconds configured for native producer linger
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Every u64 is accepted and rendered as native linger.ms; zero is admitted and disables the local producer retry delay.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One producer configuration and its native per-partition batching state.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Extreme values are delegated as decimal text; no local batch timer admission or saturation result exists.
resource_classes.release_point: Batch handoff, producer drain, producer shutdown residue transfer, or native client drop.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Every admitted linger timer belongs to one producer batch owner and is cancelled, fired, or transferred exactly once.

resource_classes.unit: milliseconds per wrapper retry delay
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Retryable immediate enqueue failure admits a Cx-aware delay based on linger_ms and 2^min(attempt,6); zero linger admits a zero-delay checkpoint and yield.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One producer submission retry loop and its originating Cx operation.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Each delay saturates and caps at 250ms, but a very large retry count has no composed elapsed-time cap.
resource_classes.release_point: Timer fire, cancellation checkpoint, nonretryable failure, success, retry exhaustion, or shutdown residue transfer.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Every admitted retry delay consumes one attempt token and one timer charge under the same operation owner.

resource_classes.unit: milliseconds supplied by the flush or close caller
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Every caller Duration is accepted; zero can return timeout immediately while extreme values can keep the wrapper loop live indefinitely in practice.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One producer flush or close invocation and all polling slices it admits.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: No local maximum or typed excessive-deadline rejection exists.
resource_classes.release_point: Drain success, elapsed wrapper budget, cancellation, panic residue transfer, or shutdown handoff.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Every polling slice decrements the same caller budget and no retry or wait phase silently resets it.

resource_classes.unit: nanoseconds per positive producer flush or close poll slice
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Zero remaining returns timeout before polling; otherwise each loop admits min(remaining,10ms), so a positive slice can be as small as one nanosecond and the native poll call is synchronous for that slice.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One slice within one producer flush or close operation.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: The slice is locally capped at 10ms, but scheduling delay and dependency behavior are not bounded by that scalar.
resource_classes.release_point: Poll return, cancellation observed by the next wrapper checkpoint, timeout exhaustion, or panic residue transfer.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: At most one slice is charged at a time and every returned slice is subtracted exactly once from its caller budget.

resource_classes.unit: milliseconds configured for native transaction operations
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Every Duration is accepted; initialization, commit, abort, and later recovery receive it only after blocking work begins, while begin_transaction has no timeout argument.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One transactional producer plus each initialization, finalization, or recovery operation receipt.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Configured-pool queue delay and fallback-slot waiting are excluded, so total future time is unbounded even when the native call receives a finite value.
resource_classes.release_point: Definitive transaction result, typed ambiguous residue transfer, cancellation before admission, or shutdown recovery handoff.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Queue wait, native call, retry or recovery, and certainty reconciliation consume one monotonic transaction deadline.

resource_classes.unit: milliseconds configured for the broker group session
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Every Duration is accepted, including zero and values unrelated to heartbeat_interval, then saturated to u64 milliseconds for native configuration.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One consumer group membership session and its assignment epoch.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Extreme values saturate for native configuration; invalid relationships are deferred to dependency behavior.
resource_classes.release_point: Group leave, eviction, consumer close, restart reconstruction, or explicit residue transfer.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Every live group session belongs to one consumer Cx owner and one assignment epoch until terminal release or transfer.

resource_classes.unit: milliseconds configured between broker heartbeats
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Every Duration is accepted and saturated to u64 milliseconds; zero and relationships inconsistent with session timeout are not rejected locally.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One consumer group membership and dependency-owned heartbeat loop.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Invalid or extreme relationships are delegated without a typed local admission result.
resource_classes.release_point: Group leave, consumer close, eviction, restart residue transfer, or dependency drop.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Every heartbeat timer is charged to one consumer group owner and cannot survive that owner's terminal receipt.

resource_classes.unit: milliseconds per synchronous commit retry delay
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Each retry derives a delay from heartbeat_interval.as_millis().max(1) using a truncating u64 cast, doubles by 2^min(attempt,6), and caps at 5000ms.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One commit operation, commit batch, assignment epoch, and originating Cx.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Durations above u64::MAX milliseconds can truncate modulo 2^64, including to zero; the 5000ms cap does not bound total retries or cloned bytes.
resource_classes.release_point: Timer fire, cancellation checkpoint, success, nonretryable failure, exhaustion, or shutdown residue transfer.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Every admitted commit retry consumes one attempt token, one batch charge, and one timer charge under one operation deadline.

resource_classes.unit: milliseconds configured between dependency-owned auto commits
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Every Duration is stored and passed to native configuration even when auto commit is disabled by default; enabling auto commit delegates the timer and pending offsets to the dependency.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One consumer and its dependency-owned pending-offset and auto-commit state.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Extreme values saturate; zero and sub-millisecond values are admitted, and no local pending-offset bound is coupled to the interval.
resource_classes.release_point: Auto-commit completion, explicit disablement, consumer close residue transfer, or dependency drop; close performs no explicit commit flush.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Every enabled timer and pending offset belongs to one consumer epoch and reaches commit, discard, or explicit residue exactly once.

resource_classes.unit: milliseconds configured as native fetch wait maximum
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Every Duration is admitted and saturated to u64 milliseconds for fetch.wait.max.ms; it is distinct from caller poll timeout and wrapper slices.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One native consumer fetch policy and dependency-owned request.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Extreme values saturate and zero is admitted; no local relation to fetch bytes or caller deadline is enforced.
resource_classes.release_point: Fetch response, dependency timeout, consumer close residue transfer, or dependency drop.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Every admitted fetch wait is owned by one request and charged within the consumer's operation policy.

resource_classes.unit: milliseconds supplied by the poll caller
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Every caller Duration is admitted; deadline conversion caps at u64 nanoseconds and zero still permits one broker poll iteration.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One consumer poll invocation, its blocking slices, buffered outcome, and assignment epoch.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Extreme durations saturate rather than reject; fallback-thread-slot wait, thread scheduling, and broker_ops mutex wait are not charged predictably to the caller budget.
resource_classes.release_point: Record or error delivery, empty timeout result, cancellation, panic residue transfer, or consumer shutdown handoff.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Every poll slice and buffered outcome belongs to one caller deadline and one assignment epoch until exactly one terminal handoff.

resource_classes.unit: milliseconds per native broker poll slice
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Each native poll uses zero or min(remaining,50ms) after it reaches the blocking closure.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One native poll slice within one caller poll operation.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: The synchronous native call receives at most 50ms, but fallback-thread-slot wait, thread scheduling, and broker_ops mutex waiting are outside that cap.
resource_classes.release_point: Native poll return, buffered outcome handoff, panic residue transfer, or shutdown reconciliation.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: At most one slice owns the shared native consumer lock at a time and every outcome remains bound to its originating poll receipt.

resource_classes.unit: milliseconds passed to each native seek call
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Every valid seek admits one blocking closure whose native seek call receives a fixed one-second timeout.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One topic-partition seek operation and its originating assignment epoch.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: Fallback-thread-slot wait, thread scheduling, and broker_ops mutex wait precede the fixed native timeout and have no local operation cap.
resource_classes.release_point: Definitive seek result, cancellation before closure entry, typed ambiguous residue transfer, or shutdown handoff.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Queue wait, mutex wait, native seek, local position update, and certainty receipt remain one operation owner.

resource_classes.unit: milliseconds hard-coded for the diagnostic consumer session
resource_classes.admission_outcome: The first diagnostic consumer construction always configures session.timeout.ms as 6000 with no caller override.
resource_classes.owner_scope: The single topic-aware consumer retained by one KafkaClient.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: No numeric overflow occurs, but the fixed dependency setting has no Cx deadline or relationship validation.
resource_classes.release_point: KafkaClient drop or explicit future diagnostic-consumer lifecycle handoff; no drain receipt exists.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: The diagnostic session timer cannot outlive its one retained consumer owner.

resource_classes.unit: topic-aware consumers retained per KafkaClient
resource_classes.admission_outcome: The first topic creates one consumer; the same topic reuses it, while a different second topic is rejected with Config.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One KafkaClient and its optional TopicAwareConsumer.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: A different topic is rejected rather than queued or replacing the existing consumer; topic bytes remain unbounded.
resource_classes.release_point: KafkaClient drop or explicit future consumer close and drain receipt.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: empty_slot + retained_consumer = exactly one slot state, and the retained topic and consumer share one owner.

resource_classes.unit: blocking closures holding or waiting for the per-consumer broker_ops mutex
resource_classes.admission_outcome: Every subscribe, rebalance, poll, commit, seek, or close closure can wait for the same mutex without an operation-Cx checkpoint; successfully spawned closures share the 256-thread counter, excess callers wait earlier under K1R-024, and OS spawn failure runs a closure inline after decrementing that counter.
resource_classes.owner_scope: One KafkaConsumer native backend plus every originating operation receipt queued behind broker_ops.
resource_classes.overflow_behavior: The mutex admits one holder, but its aggregate holder/waiter population has no frozen cap because inline closures bypass the spawned-thread counter; excess pre-spawn callers also wait without typed saturation under K1R-024.
resource_classes.release_point: Mutex acquisition followed by closure completion or panic; caller future cancellation can discard the result without interrupting an executing or mutex-waiting closure.
resource_classes.accounting_invariant: Every admitted mutex waiter remains charged to its originating operation until acquisition and terminal closure accounting or explicit shutdown residue transfer.

lifecycle_operations.entry_admission: Synchronous construction validates configuration and delegates native client, connection, queue, callback, and thread admission without Cx ownership or a constructor deadline.

transitions.current_rule: No constructor timeout is exposed; dependency delay is not charged to a Cx deadline.
No Cx parameter or cancellation transition exists.
Drop is the observed release boundary; no explicit producer shutdown or dependency-drain receipt is required.
No constructor or lifetime panic guard produces resource accounting.
Caller may construct a new object; no shared retry budget or prior-residue join exists.
No persisted connection, request, delivery, or residue state is reconciled after process restart.
Native side effects and background resources are not represented by a typed ownership receipt.

lifecycle_operations.release_accounting: Construction success transfers all native resources to one client owner; failure, panic, drop, and restart must account for every partially admitted resource.

lifecycle_operations.entry_admission: Entry checks Cx, validates topic and payload, reserves an uncapped active-operation count, and delegates queue admission; topic, key, headers, framing, and queue bytes remain uncapped.

transitions.current_rule: request_timeout does not directly bound wrapper admission, backoff, or delivery await.
Entry or backoff cancellation is pre-effect; cancellation after enqueue closes local receiver ownership but cannot retract the record or stop its callback.
Close fences later admission but an already admitted send can finish or remain dependency-owned during drain.
The active-operation guard releases locally, but delivery and dependency queue ownership may survive unwinding.
Only immediate retryable enqueue errors use the wrapper count; callback errors do not retry, and dependency retries are separately configured.
No persisted delivery receipt or idempotent replay decision survives process restart.
The callback can be discarded after caller cancellation and no typed delivery-certainty state exists.

lifecycle_operations.release_accounting: Every successful enqueue retains one record charge and one receipt owner until a definitive callback or explicit ambiguous-delivery handoff.
